migration: Pure pursuit geometry was ported to a ROS-independent C++ controller; the ROS 2 adapter implements planner_msgs/PathFollower, fresh odometry validation, cancellation, terminal heading alignment, and zero-command shutdown handling.
terminal_pose_adaptation: ROS 2 terminal heading alignment uses hysteresis: enter at position tolerance, leave beyond 1.5 times that tolerance or on aligned heading with remaining position error. Success still requires both original position and yaw tolerances. While aligning, bounded body-X position feedback (2/s) and measured body-velocity damping (0.5) oppose turn-induced motion; correction is capped at min(active_speed, 0.1 m/s). Angular command remains bounded 2/s yaw feedback. These are adapter controls separate from the upstream pure-pursuit velocity law. Ordinary rotation-only tracking also has the longitudinal hold adaptation documented below; no lateral velocity control or physical-model equivalence is claimed.
terminal_velocity_integral_adaptation: Explicit optional ROS 2 improvement, not an upstream algorithm. terminal_velocity_integral_gain defaults to 0 and exactly preserves the existing stateless command. A nonnegative gain integrates the longitudinal velocity error ((4/3)*body_goal_x - measured_body_vx) using the fixed control period. The integral is bounded by the existing terminal linear limit and freezes when its error pushes an already saturated command farther into saturation; opposite errors can unwind it. Integration runs only in ALIGNING and resets on mode exit, a new goal, cancellation, completion or shutdown. The integral and applied gain are exposed in tracking status. Position/yaw success thresholds, alignment exit distance, ordinary pure pursuit, angular control and physical parameters are unchanged. Longitudinal compensation does not guarantee lateral-slip rejection or terminal convergence.
terminal_position_recovery_adaptation: On each Aligning-to-Tracking exit, latch forward/reverse from the goal body-X sign; retain it through that recovery episode and clear it on alignment reentry, reaching the goal, cancellation or a new goal. In terminal recovery only, use alpha=wrap(goal bearing-current yaw-reverse*pi), w=clamp(2*alpha,+/-max_ang_vel), and v=0 until abs(alpha)<critical_angle, then v=direction*min(active_speed,0.1,2*rho)*max(0,cos(alpha)). With translation permitted, set only w to zero when direction*body_goal_x>0 and abs(body_goal_y)<the actual configured position tolerance: the current travel ray can already enter that existing XY disk. The original v, critical-angle guard, position/yaw success criteria and 1.5-times alignment exit distance remain in force. The node passes goal_reaching_threshold; the retained six-argument API and explicit zero-tolerance calls preserve the preceding bearing command for existing tools. These are ROS 2 terminal recovery controls, not upstream algorithm claims. The path controller advances once per tick for metrics and carrot publication.
rotation_only_hold_adaptation: During one ordinary pursuit rotation_only episode, latch the entry XY and replace only its zero linear command with clamp(2*body_anchor_x-0.5*measured_body_vx, +/-min(active_speed,0.1)). Preserve the pursuit angular command unless the separately documented optional rotation_hold_yaw_governor is enabled. Reset the anchor on leaving that episode, terminal alignment or recovery, a new goal, cancellation, completion and shutdown. Translation and other ordinary pursuit branches keep their pursuit commands. This ROS 2 chassis adaptation counters longitudinal contact drift through cmd_vel; it does not actuate lateral motion or modify vehicle physics, path tubes or success tolerances.

rotation_only_hold_validation.comparison: Independent cold starts on the original Edgar mesh and recorded 192-point motion5 route: old first-turn XY displacement 0.14713 m, hold 0.08666 m. Old first violates the unchanged 0.15 m path tube at 2.04 s; hold has no offline PathProgress violation, but neither reaches the terminal pose in the 60 s budget. Rotation-only hold is inactive after terminal entry. Historical contact/wheel state, ROS Actions and online mapping are not restored.

terminal_disk_entry_validation.comparison: One hold_straight cold start on the same original mesh and 192-point route, with no gain sweep or baseline rerun. All fields shared with the existing hold CSV match until 24.6 s, when only recovery requested_w first differs. Reaches at 36.4 s with XY error 0.02428535 m and absolute yaw error 0.0862945 rad under the original 0.04 m/0.1 rad criteria. Maximum route XYZ error is 0.09923387 m, offline PathProgress reports no violation, all 18201 observations have four wheel contacts and zero chassis contacts. Four alignment entries and three recoveries replace the recorded hold loop. This is isolated core evidence, not full ROS mission acceptance or post-stop settling validation.

terminal_recovery_validation.comparison: Same recorded first-alignment path with fresh settled Bullet initial state: latched-pursuit recovery 29.45 s, direct position recovery 20.40 s. Historical wheel/contact state is not restored; this is not the full exploration mission.

status_sampling: tracking_status is an event stream on transitions, not periodic telemetry. Transitions publish after this tick applies its command; odometry_stamp_s identifies the observation. tracking_state service returns a current snapshot.
corner_preservation_adaptation: Optional preserve_corners defaults to false and retains the legacy upstream carrot/path-consumption branch when disabled. When enabled, identify nonzero XY tangent turns >= the existing critical_angle while skipping consecutive duplicate XY samples. Store original corner indices independently of measured-prefix pruning. The first pending corner bounds both closest-waypoint search and carrot selection until measured XY enters its existing goal_reaching_threshold disk; selecting a carrot never deletes the preceding unvisited geometry. Only measured nearest-point pruning advances the retained route prefix. Command exposes corner_limited and pending_corners, and tracking status exposes preserve_corners. While a gate remains, the node resets/defers terminal alignment and success, and the core suppresses endpoint position_reached, so a returning route cannot finish near its start before visiting its corners. Releasing the final gate allows ordinary terminal policy on the next tick. While a gate remains, the approach scaling distance is max(final endpoint XY distance, pending gate XY distance). This prevents a returning route from stalling at its coincident endpoint without treating a corner as a new stopping destination. If the endpoint is farther than the gate, its existing slowdown is retained exactly; after the last gate, ordinary endpoint approach resumes. Radius/curvature scaling, velocity limits, rotation-only hold, critical angle, position/yaw criteria and route tube are unchanged. This changes upstream route-consumption semantics and is a ROS 2 geometry adaptation, not upstream equivalence.

corner_preservation_diagnosis.finding: motion7 third local route: all 168 interpolated points are initially within 0.5 m; legacy chooses the endpoint and deletes the 107.975-degree corner on its first step. All 74 distinct later translation commands match endpoint-only PP within 6e-8. Initial rotation drift is only 0.01231 m. At cancellation the global nearest original XYZ route distance is 0.150161 m, matching PathProgress without a cursor restriction; even the ideal endpoint chord leaves the original 0.15 m tube. This is saved-data evidence of corner cutting, not candidate physics or full mission acceptance.

corner_approach_validation.finding: Before/after C++ cores each evaluate the same 36 fixed observed poses; nine directed checks pass. A closed square starts with 0.2 m/s instead of zero and also starts in reverse when headed backward. Gate/carrot/completion results are identical for all observations. Legacy, no-corner, rotation-only, near-gate endpoint-dominated and post-final-gate commands are identical in these cases. This is a controller check, not a closed-loop vehicle convergence claim.
corner_approach_validation.motion7_scope: The previously successful 28.65 s motion7 cold-start replay predates this approach change. The original route geometry and gate ordering are unchanged; commands can change only while a gate remains and its distance exceeds the final endpoint distance. The prior physical time/trajectory must not be claimed as a validation of the new velocity sequence.

rotation_hold_yaw_governor_adaptation: Optional ROS 2 chassis command adaptation, not an upstream algorithm. rotation_hold_yaw_governor defaults false in the node and is explicitly true in SMB configuration. During the existing ordinary rotation_only hold episode and terminal ALIGNING, use the shared longitudinalYawScale function: e_x=(target-current) projected onto current body X, gamma=clamp(1-abs(e_x)/goal_reaching_threshold,0,1). For ordinary turning the target is the episode anchor; for terminal alignment it is the endpoint. Multiply only the original angular command by gamma; keep each branch longitudinal law and integral unchanged. Original RotationOnlyHold::step remains; governedStep exposes v,w,gamma and e_x. Anchor reset lifecycle, terminal position-recovery branch, ordinary translation, yaw-direction choice, original success and collision tolerances, and physical parameters are unchanged. No direction latching is added. Vehicle yaw slew and integral feedback still govern actual wheel demands; requested zero yaw is not instantaneous zero applied yaw. Body-X attenuation does not actuate lateral motion or guarantee full-pose convergence.
rotation_hold_yaw_governor_diagnosis: results/edgar_mine/motion9_tracking_analysis.json reconstructs 270 distinct saved commands with max residual 3.25e-7. Motion9 released the first two substantial gates, then stayed rotation_only toward the third gate. Anchor hold was active but drift reached 0.23716 m. With v=+0.1 m/s, actual body vx was often approximately -0.1 m/s while yaw feedback applied -1 rad/s to differential wheel targets. Only later did body-goal-X crossings trigger two yaw sign changes. Existing core/source hashes match run provenance. This motivates allowing longitudinal recovery by reducing yaw; it does not prove the candidate works.

rotation_hold_yaw_governor_validation.result: One independent cold start on motion9 exact 301-point path and original mesh, no live-baseline rerun or sweep: all pending corners release by 27.5 s, maximum route XYZ distance 0.0768442 m, original PathProgress has no violation, all 30001 observations have four wheel contacts and zero chassis contacts. Ordinary rotation hold anchor displacement stays within 0.0316909 m; 163/167 hold ticks attenuate yaw. The 60 s candidate does not reach the full terminal pose: XY error 0.0483605 m, yaw error 1.6124773 rad. After first terminal entry at 39.65 s, original terminal alignment/recovery is entered seven times with six exits to recovery; the new governor is inactive there. Physical full-path acceptance is therefore not claimed. Historical wheel/contact state, ROS and online mapping are not replayed.
rotation_hold_yaw_governor_validation.scope: The first candidate applies the governor only during ordinary rotation. It is preserved as a failed terminal-convergence baseline; the distinct terminal-alignment extension is recorded separately below. No unchanged baseline or parameter sweep was run.

terminal_yaw_governor_validation.comparison: Apply the same governor additionally to terminal ALIGNING, keeping all other laws, route, physics and tolerances unchanged. The 39 shared CSV columns match the saved ordinary-governor candidate to 1e-12 until 39.65 s; then only governor_yaw_scale and requested_w first differ. The old candidate is not rerun.
terminal_yaw_governor_validation.result: At 60 s, still not reached: XY error 0.0372390 m is within 0.04 m, yaw error 0.621632 rad exceeds 0.1 rad. ALIGNING entries decrease from 7 to 3 and exits to recovery from 6 to 2. Both exits correctly exceed the existing 0.06 m hysteresis radius; both recovery episodes retain direction -1. All three entries satisfy the existing 0.04 m disk. No terminal-state or direction-latch error is observed. Final requested w=0.225292, slew-limited w=0.227843, feedback-applied w=0.625786 and actual body wz=0.286400 rad/s; the body is still turning toward the target, which is not proof of later success.
terminal_yaw_governor_validation.path_and_contact: Original frozen PathProgress reports no violation; maximum route XYZ distance 0.0833054 m. All 30001 samples have four-wheel contact and zero chassis contact. The ordinary-rotation segment is identical to the previous candidate and all gates release by 27.5 s.
terminal_yaw_governor_validation.scope: No extra duration or third candidate was run. Historical contact/wheel state, ROS Actions and online mapping are absent; full native mission remains necessary.

steering_curvature_adaptation.law: Moving branch: w=clamp(2*v*y/(x*x+y*y), +/-max_ang_vel), using the final signed v and the same body-frame carrot.
steering_curvature_adaptation.reason: The upstream +0.01 radius regularizer produces a nonzero steering command for arbitrarily small lateral error. Recorded Pittsburgh autonomy2 first v=.3,w=-.0235271 matches that bias; real steering precedes drift.
steering_curvature_adaptation.retained: Original linear-speed scaling, carrot selection, critical-angle rotation branch, corner retention, rotation hold, terminal policy, route tube, physical model and limits.
steering_curvature_adaptation.scope: ROS 2 tracking adaptation, not an upstream algorithm-equivalence claim. Runtime mode is exposed in tracking status.

steering_curvature_validation.whole_mission_result: failed: subsequent local path invalidated as path_not_free at revision46; stopped and replanned, then ground_root_unknown until the observation deadline. No completed local cycle or homing.
steering_curvature_validation.comparison_scope: Independent native runs support the specific straight-search completion claim, not a matched-observation speedup or success rate.

ground_maneuver_core.provenance: New ROS2 extension; not extracted upstream pure-pursuit logic.
ground_maneuver_core.scope: Standalone closed-loop straight/pivot controller with explicit signed primitive geometry, observed settling and bounded acceleration for feedback and stopping.
ground_maneuver_core.runtime: Separate installed library and model demo, now consumed only by the explicitly enabled GROUND_MANEUVER Action mode. PATH remains the default and does not run this controller.
ground_maneuver_core.reference_model: q=base+offset*heading is an explicit approved-reference hypothesis; actual observations drive feedback and completion.
ground_maneuver_core.remaining_integration: The upstream PCI and follower own task admission, real ValidatePath calls, original route progress and live remaining-reference checks. Tracker validates transport/reference consistency and actual starting state; these checks are not substitutes for map validation.

ground_maneuver_action.provenance: New opt-in ROS2 extension, not upstream pure-pursuit equivalence.
ground_maneuver_action.interface: PathFollower.execution_mode=GROUND_MANEUVER with GroundManeuver and indexed GroundManeuverSegment messages. Pose path, reference time and endpoint velocities are retained, with explicit signed primitive amounts and stopped boundaries.
ground_maneuver_action.admission: allow_ground_maneuver defaults false. Reject nonmanual violations, malformed arrays, nonfinite values, reference/primitive inconsistencies, speed/acceleration/time/path caps, moving or mismatched start. pre_execution_timeout is remaining wall admission budget and is not renewed between accept and accepted.
ground_maneuver_action.execution: The existing tracking node remains the only Twist publisher. Actual odometry drives straight/pivot feedback, signed accumulated turn completion and three fresh stopped observations. Reference time never skips a primitive. No recovery route is synthesized.
ground_maneuver_action.clock: Core motion budgets and acceleration use monotonic ROS motion time. Wall receipt loss aborts. Stale transport is inhibited to zero when ROS time is paused; this emergency pause inhibition is not stop confirmation. A resumed output is additionally slew-limited in ROS time. A separate finite wall stop watchdog reports unconfirmed failure if observations cannot confirm the stop.
ground_maneuver_action.default: Ordinary PATH goals retain their pure-pursuit route, speed inheritance and terminal policy. Maneuver goals do not rewrite the stored ordinary-path speed.
ground_maneuver_action.validation_scope: Implementation and model checks are separate from native mission acceptance; no native success is asserted here.

ground_route_crossings.provenance: New opt-in ground-route execution obligation, not an upstream pure-pursuit feature.
ground_route_crossings.contract: An approved STRAIGHT primitive can require ordered interior distances. Its endpoint still requires stationary confirmation. Crossings use original intermediate 0.01 m / 0.02 rad bounds, positive measured progress and new source observations; missed obligations brake rather than skip.
ground_route_crossings.transport: GroundManeuverSegment.pass_through_distances is preserved through the PathFollower bridge and independently validated by the tracking node. Maximum 64 crossings per plan.
ground_route_crossings.status: Core and wire implementation built; per-odometry crossing reception fix in progress after recorded 20 Hz sampling miss. No new native physics result.
